description: Machine-readable rules learned from past engagements. Each subagent reads its own section at the start of every run and applies the rules at the points documented in its agent .md. Rules are appended by /retro apply; never edit by hand unless you know what you're doing — /forget will land in v1.5. CONFIDENCE CONVENTION: low/medium are self-judged (analyze-mode retros). `high` is reserved for rules grounded in EXTERNAL TRUTH and MUST carry a `grounding` field — either `platform_disposition:<report-id>` (a triager verdict, via /outcome) or `user_policy` (an explicit operator directive). Run scripts/bb_rule_audit.py to flag self-judged-high rules, missing provenance, dup IDs, stale refs to disabled rules, and filter:discovery drift. Disabled rules keep `enabled:false` + a `disabled_reason` as cautionary records (not deleted).

in_scope_subdomain_override.reason: Added at takeover-hunter integration time. Subdomains under in-scope wildcards are owned by zone-control proof; without this override every takeover-hunter candidate would land at 'unknown' verdict for dangling subdomains that lack Wayback presence (typical, since the program already stopped linking them) and lack GH code-search hits (also typical, since dangling subdomains aren't actively referenced in code). High-confidence ownership case structurally — no third party can impersonate a record under the program's own DNS zone.

bucket_ownership_positive_proof_required.applies_when: asset_class == bucket_name AND a report is being considered (verified-listable bucket headed toward an owned verdict)
bucket_ownership_positive_proof_required.rationale: S3 bucket names are globally unique first-come-first-served. Name-derivation from an in-scope host, a third-party repo referencing the bucket, and brand-plausible content are ALL squatter-compatible and prove nothing about ownership. The content gate (44212/82369) is a NEGATIVE filter (off-brand content -> unowned); it passes brand-plausible squats. Ownership of a bucket therefore requires POSITIVE proof, not merely the absence of disconfirming content.
positive_proofs_any_one_suffices: DNS CNAME chain from a confirmed in-scope host resolves to <bucket>.s3[.region].amazonaws.com (the host->bucket binding is verified, not assumed)
the bucket is referenced in a FIRST-PARTY repo/config — a repo under a confirmed program-owned GitHub org — NOT a third-party repo
the bucket name is explicitly listed in program scope
the bucket returns an object/key whose content is uniquely and unambiguously program-proprietary (internal project names, employee identifiers, program-specific data schemas)
non_proofs_explicit: name strictly derives from an in-scope host stem (REVOKED rule 951ed)
a third-party / external GitHub repo references the bucket
bucket content is merely brand-plausible (e.g. UUID PNGs consistent with an upload service) without being uniquely program-proprietary
bucket virtual-host resolves (every existing bucket resolves regardless of owner)
bucket_ownership_positive_proof_required.if_no_positive_proof: set verdict=unknown (NOT owned); /draft-report then refuses per the standard owned-gate. Surface to operator as 'listable but ownership-unprovable' — do not draft.

bucket_ownership_positive_proof_required.reason: GROUND TRUTH: H1 #3766855 (api-staging-uploads) closed NOT APPLICABLE by bucket-specialist triager matthew_bryant — 'I see no evidence that Airtable owns this bucket.' The report rested on name-derivation + a third-party repo's staging.env + brand-plausible UUID-PNG content — all squatter-compatible. No CNAME chain and no first-party reference were ever established. This is the loop's first triager-disposition-driven rule, hence confidence=high (vs the self-judged medium ceiling). Supersedes revoked 951ed and complements the negative content-gate 82369.

subdomain_name_fingerprint_required.reason: glpi.mutazuay.com was not running GLPI — the DNS label was a legacy name for a service that was replaced; fingerprinting before CVE pivot is mandatory to avoid chasing wrong-application vulnerabilities.

refuse_if_explicit_scanner_ban.reason: subzy + subzy_body_recheck curl gates issue direct HTTP requests to program subdomains; any automated HTTP scanning against program infrastructure is prohibited when explicit_scanner_ban is set

refuse_if_explicit_scanner_ban_provenanc.reason: Agent-side enforcement mirror of the parser-side explicit_scanner_ban flag; without this gate an operator who forgets to check the flag would run subzy HTTP probes against a program with a categorical automated-scanning ban.

subzy_body_recheck_required.fingerprint_assertion: Live HTTP response body MUST contain the can-i-take-over-xyz fingerprint string for the matched service. If body is empty, 0 bytes, or contains a generic webserver default (nginx default 404, Apache default 403, AWS S3 NoSuchBucket XML, Cloudflare 'Site not Configured', SendGrid edge 404, etc.), the candidate is a subzy false positive and must be disqualified before passing to report-drafter.

known_false_positive_patterns.live_body_observed: HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found served by nginx (SendGrid edge), 146-byte body containing only the nginx default 404 template
known_false_positive_patterns.reason: SendGrid sender-authentication CNAMEs return plain nginx 404 from SendGrid's edge. SendGrid CNAMEs are not user-claimable (tied to authenticated accounts via API keys + ownership verification), so even if subzy's fingerprint matched coincidentally, no exploitable takeover scenario exists.

subzy_body_recheck_required.reason: Subzy's fingerprint match against can-i-take-over-xyz is a single passive GET at scan time; the fingerprint database has stale/loose patterns and false-positive overlap with generic 404 pages. Confirmed FP in bc-seek 15705866.careerfair.jobstreet.com: subzy claimed Cargo Collective dangling, but live body is plain nginx 404 from SendGrid edge — no Cargo branding, no claimable binding. Without this gate the takeover-hunter pipeline propagates FPs through ownership-verifier and report-drafter (no live verification was done at any stage in v1) and ships a false-positive report. Symmetric to bucket_hunter.s3scanner_acl_recheck_required which catches the same class of FP on bucket-listing claims.
subzy_body_recheck_required.reason_provenance: bc-seek 15705866.careerfair.jobstreet.com flagged VULNERABLE by subzy on the Cargo Collective fingerprint. Post-draft live verification returned plain nginx 404 from SendGrid edge, no Cargo branding in body, CNAME target is sendgrid.net (sender-authentication leftover, not a Cargo Collective hostname), and SendGrid CNAMEs are structurally not user-claimable. Single confirmed FP today; confidence kept at medium pending future corroboration (mirror of s3scanner ACL gate which is also at medium).

cname_hub_skip.reason: 34 bild.de campaign subdomains (100euro.bild.de, 150.bild.de, 12monate.bild.de, etc.) all CNAME to swerve.bild.de which is a live Bild-owned internal redirect mesh — none are individually dangling.

57 welt.de subdomains CNAME-delegate to schneevonmorgen.com (Damoh ad platform) which is fully live and claimed — this is a normal CDN/ad-tech delegation pattern, not an exploitable dangling endpoint.

80 of 87 bc-seek CNAMEs resolved to *.cdn.cloudflare.net; Cloudflare Anycast is always live so these can never be dangling takeover candidates; suffix match on cdn.cloudflare.net drops all of them before subzy.

2 subdomains in int-watsons CNAME to suiteN.emarsys.net; subzy flagged both as Unbounce VULNERABLE; body recheck showed Emarsys is live (302 to suite{N}.emarsys.net/docroot.html, x-af suite headers). Emarsys is a SAP enterprise service, structurally not user-claimable. Adding as cname_hub_skip suffix prevents wasting subzy capacity and prevents Unbounce FP propagation.
54/60 CNAMEs resolve to wc.shopify.com (Shopify's own live redirect mesh); hub-skip would have cut subzy input from 60 to 6 and prevented the one FP that still required two rules to discharge.

4 of 33 CNAME chains in this engagement resolved to *.impervadns.net (Imperva internal nameserver tree); hub-skip would have cut subzy input by 4 and prevented the Cargo FP on img.capital.com from needing body-recheck discharge.

3 Chime sender-authentication subdomains (email.news, email.rally, email.talent) all CNAME to mailgun.org; Mailgun sender-auth CNAMEs are account-bound and structurally not user-claimable — parallel to SendGrid cname_hub_skip; adding as suffix drops all mailgun.org CNAMEs before subzy.
cname_hub_skip.rationale: Mailgun sender-auth CNAMEs (account-bound, verified-domain-required) cannot be claimed by third parties; 3 firings confirm mailgun.org suffix is a reliable hub-skip candidate.

cname_hub_skip.reason: CloudFront distributions (*.cloudfront.net CNAMEs) are live AWS CDN infrastructure and structurally not user-claimable; subzy fired Cargo Collective VULNERABLE on clicks.anchor.fm (CNAME d3p8mhf5vuafd9.cloudfront.net) in spotify engagement — 4th Cargo FP corroboration; suffix-skip prevents subzy capacity waste on all CloudFront CNAMEs
cname_hub_skip.rationale: AWS CloudFront distributions require AWS-account ownership to create/claim; a *.cloudfront.net CNAME can never be taken over by an attacker registering a new distribution — the distribution ID in the CNAME is the account-bound handle. Body recheck in this engagement confirmed: live openresty 404 from the distribution, no Cargo Collective branding. Adding cloudfront.net suffix to cname_hub_skip eliminates an entire class of subzy noise (parallel to the existing cdn.cloudflare.net and impervadns.net entries).

cname_hub_skip.reason: 6 subdomains resolved to live aswatson ELB targets; the AWS ELB hub-skip is the upstream prevention rather than relying on the downstream Cargo FP discharge rule — parallel to the existing cloudfront.net and impervadns.net hub-skip entries.
2 Marionnaud subdomains resolved to Akamai EdgeKey CDN targets which are live account-bound infrastructure; adding the suffix drops them before subzy wastes probes on non-dangling CDN endpoints.

subzy_known_fp_patterns.reason: Cargo Collective fingerprint fires on generic Apache 404 served from AWS ELB CNAME target. Observed: m.newsletter.watsons.com.tr CNAME aswatson-prod1-ssl-req-157263-151311547.eu-west-1.elb.amazonaws.com. Extends prior bc-seek SendGrid FP class to AWS ELB hosts.
subzy_known_fp_patterns.reason_provenance: m.newsletter.watsons.com.tr CNAMEs to an AWS ELB host; subzy flagged Cargo Collective VULNERABLE but live body was a generic Apache 404 with zero Cargo branding — same FP mechanism as bc-seek/SendGrid, showing the Cargo fingerprint fires on any bare 404 irrespective of the hosting platform.

subzy_known_fp_patterns.live_body_signature: Emarsys SAP 404 page (x-af/x-hf headers, 302 to suiteN.emarsys.net/docroot.html; no Unbounce branding)
subzy_known_fp_patterns.reason: Unbounce fingerprint fires on Emarsys SAP email platform generic 404. Two corroborations in one engagement: suite16.emarsys.net (link.watsons.com.tr) and suite40.emarsys.net (links.reg.watsons.com.hk). Emarsys is not user-claimable; SAP enterprise service.
subzy_known_fp_patterns.reason_provenance: Two independent Emarsys suite CNAMEs (suite16 and suite40) both triggered subzy's Unbounce fingerprint in the same engagement; live body recheck in both cases showed live Emarsys SAP service headers and no Unbounce branding — dual corroboration in a single run.

subzy_known_fp_patterns.reason: Third consecutive engagement (bc-seek SendGrid, int-watsons ELB, shopify PaaS) confirms Cargo fingerprint fires on any bare 404; a wildcard endpoint pattern subsumes all three per-platform entries and prevents future one-off additions.

subzy_known_fp_patterns.live_body_signature: 19-byte Go http.NotFound() body (text/plain 'page not found'; no Uptimerobot branding)
subzy_known_fp_patterns.reason: Uptimerobot fingerprint fires on Go http.NotFound() (19 bytes, text/plain) served from Mailgun sender-authentication CNAMEs. 3 corroborations in one engagement: email.news.chime.com, email.rally.chime.com, email.talent.chime.com. Mailgun sender-auth CNAMEs are structurally not user-claimable (account-bound).
subzy_known_fp_patterns.rationale: Uptimerobot fingerprint string 'page not found' matches Go's http.NotFound() body served by Mailgun's edge on 3 independent email.*.chime.com CNAMEs; parallel to the Cargo+SendGrid FP class in bc-seek.

subzy_known_fp_patterns.live_body_signature: HTTP 200 Next.js app (Vercel server, x-vercel-cache HIT; Gemfury string appears only in compiled JS bundle 404 component)
subzy_known_fp_patterns.reason: Gemfury fingerprint string 'This page could not be found.' appears in compiled Next.js JS bundles as the framework-default 404 component; any Vercel-hosted Next.js app will falsely trigger this fingerprint regardless of whether it is a dangling Gemfury endpoint.

amass_cap_warning_threshold.warning_text: amass produced {count} unique subdomains not covered by subfinder+crtsh that were unavailable under the strict subdomain cap; on future revisit consider running takeover-hunter with a higher cap
amass_cap_warning_threshold.reason: kiwicom: 868 amass-unique subs (511 kiwi.com + 357 skypicker.com) unavailable under 100-sub strict cap; the strict cap is per-program-policy but the wasted coverage warrants operator notification

amass_cap_warning_threshold_provenance.reason: amass ran in parallel and found 868 unique subs not in subfinder+crtsh that were structurally unavailable under the 100-sub strict cap filled by round-robin alphabetical subfinder+crtsh results; an operator warning threshold prevents silent funnel-narrowing on high-subdomain-count programs.

slug_dir_hygiene.rationale: Always derive the output path from program["slug"] in the program JSON — never reuse a sibling or prior engagement slug. Observed bug: mutualistaazuay run wrote takeovers to out/mutazuay/takeovers/ and referenced wrong slug in verify call.
slug_dir_hygiene.check: Before writing any output file, assert os.path.basename(output_dir) == program["slug"] from the loaded program JSON.
slug_dir_hygiene.reason: takeover-hunter wrote output to out/mutazuay/takeovers/ instead of out/mutualistaazuay/takeovers/ — wrong sibling-engagement slug used for both file path and verify-ownership call; requires the subagent to derive output dir strictly from program JSON slug.

auto_info_filter.reason: Local filesystem paths must never appear in submitted bug-bounty reports. They leak researcher tooling internals and directory structure to the program triager, give competing researchers operational intel, can subtly bias triagers against the finding (looks like automated/scripted submission), and reveal internal classifier/rule identifiers that add nothing to the technical case.
auto_info_filter.reason_provenance: User direct policy instruction 2026-05-16, given twice: 'In the next reports do not include this local information like: Cache: memory/ownership-cache/00a486a91e889634.json. Those sort of thinks referring local paths of my system'. High confidence because explicit user policy, not inferred heuristic. The Automattic bundled report (H1 #3741482) shipped with 6 such leaks before this rule existed — exactly the failure mode this rule prevents going forward.

severity_overrides.match_condition: leaked-secret candidate whose detector is a blockchain RPC provider (Alchemy, Infura, QuickNode, Ankr, Moralis, GetBlock, Chainstack, Pokt/Grove, or any JSON-RPC endpoint key) — EVEN IF trufflehog Verified==true
elevation_requires_all: the key is demonstrably NOT a public/client-side dApp project ID (i.e. not committed in browser-shipped frontend code where exposure is by design)
the key is NOT free-tier and NOT a test/e2e fixture (check surrounding file: compose.yml, e2e_tests/, *.test.*, simulator, DISABLE_AUTH flags, etc.)
the key demonstrably grants capability beyond public-chain JSON-RPC reads (e.g. private tx broadcast, webhook/admin management) — and that capability is shown, not speculated
severity_overrides.rationale: trufflehog Verified==true proves only that the ISSUER accepts the credential, NOT that it carries security impact. Blockchain RPC keys are frequently public-by-design (browser dApps expose project IDs), free-tier, or test fixtures, and grant at most rate-limit consumption against PUBLIC chains. Default them low and route to manual triage instead of auto-drafting High.
severity_overrides.reason: GROUND TRUTH: H1 #3742794 (worldcoin Alchemy+Infura keys) closed DUPLICATE; program's own assessment surfaced by triager h1_analyst_anya — Alchemy key 'just for testing services' without significant security impact (#3020852), Infura key 'on a free plan and no longer being used by our simulator' (#3543111). Both were trufflehog-verified-live yet low/no-impact. The loop has surfaced this exact key class repeatedly (chainlink: 15 verified Infura/Alchemy; okg: Infura/OKLink) — now ground-truth-confirmed as low-value. Confidence=high because grounded in a program disposition, not self-judgment.

severity_overrides.match_condition: ANY leaked-secret or exposed-asset report where the impact section asserts a capability that was not directly observed
severity_overrides.requirement: Impact statements must describe only capabilities demonstrated by the evidence at hand. State the confirmed impact plainly; if a higher impact is conditional, omit it rather than speculate — triagers read speculative escalation as inflation and it can bias the whole report down.
severity_overrides.reason: The H1 #3742794 report inflated a free-tier/test RPC key with speculative capabilities — 'request interception', 'World ID proof interception', 'higher-privilege methods (private tx broadcasting, webhook management) MAY also be available'. None are granted by blockchain JSON-RPC keys. The speculative framing did not survive contact with a triager who knew the keys were test/free-tier. Confirmed alongside rule-report_drafter-blockchain_rpc_key_severity_cap-7c4d9.

vendor_credential_attribution_override.reason: The strongest finding (live billing-enabled Maps key) would have been blocked by the owned gate because it lives in a vendor repo scored unowned; credential attribution to the scope owner via deploy context is the correct ownership signal for directed engagements.

cve_patch_date_gate.condition: cve_fix_release_date is known AND app_build_date > cve_fix_release_date
cve_patch_date_gate.reasoning: When the application build date is later than the CVE fix release date, the build is almost certainly patched. Build recency (a recent build date) does NOT imply unpatched status — it implies the opposite for CVEs with known fix dates. Always anchor the patched/vulnerable verdict to: (fix_release_date <= app_build_date) => likely patched; (app_build_date < fix_release_date) => possibly unpatched.
cve_patch_date_gate.example: CVE-2025-29927 fix shipped Next.js 15.2.3 on 2025-03-XX. React 19 canary build dated 2025-12-17 in glpi.mutazuay.com is post-fix => correctly concluded patched. Confirmed by status-code-only middleware bypass test (all 307->login, bypass did not fire).
cve_patch_date_gate.reason: The initial CVE-2025-29927 assessment for glpi.mutazuay.com incorrectly reasoned that a December 2025 build 'may be unpatched' when in fact the fix shipped in March 2025; correcting this reasoning at the rule level prevents future report drafts from flagging false CVE findings based on build recency alone.

require_cap_refinement_when_all_caps_unk.reason: Bugcrowd dump via arkadiyt/bounty-targets-data does not carry per-target severity caps; all caps default to unknown which causes report_drafter severity min(proposed, cap) to silently downgrade every finding to medium

All 44 bc-monash-mbb assets have severity_cap=unknown due to Bugcrowd parser limitation; without this gate, any drafted report would have its severity silently capped at medium regardless of actual impact.

severity_cap_synthesized_override.note: For direct/owner-authorized engagements with a SYNTHESIZED scope, severity_cap is a conservative default — not an authoritative program ceiling. Rate the finding by actual impact and document the override reason. First observed: mutualistaazuay Azure subdomain takeover rated High despite medium cap.
severity_cap_synthesized_override.reason: mutualistaazuay synthesized scope defaulted severity_cap=medium; the Azure subdomain takeover on a financial brand warrants High by impact — the synthesized cap was a placeholder, not an authoritative ceiling; report_drafter must not mechanically apply synthesized caps.

detect_phrases: cannot accept any submissions found by using automatic scanners
explicit_scanner_ban.set_true_when: any of detect_phrases found in policy with explicit prohibition language
explicit_scanner_ban.effect: orchestrator must skip hunt-takeovers; treated as a stronger gate than automated_tools_allowed=false for any agent issuing direct HTTP requests to program subdomains

explicit_scanner_ban_provenance.reason: UZ Leuven policy verbatim: 'We cannot accept any submissions found by using automatic scanners' — operator had to manually catch this before running hunt-takeovers; parser should detect and set the flag automatically at ingestion time.

rate_limit_cap_rps.note: when policy explicitly states a rate cap lower than the default 10 req/sec, store it in rules.rate_limit_cap_rps so all agents that issue HTTP requests respect the tighter bound

rate_limit_cap_rps_provenance.reason: UZ Leuven policy states 'max. 5 requests /sec'; this was captured in the rules.notes free-text field but not as a machine-readable cap that agents can enforce automatically — parser should extract it at ingestion time.

wayback_confidence_ceiling.reason: Three archive-derived candidates (Telerik CVE, Yii2 debug, banking IDOR paths) were presented at high/medium confidence from Wayback pattern-match alone; all three cleared on live GET — archive-only provenance must be a hard confidence ceiling of low/needs-live-check.

long_exposure_duplicate_prior.applies_when: an exposed-endpoint/service candidate has multi-year archive history (Wayback/CommonCrawl earliest snapshot > ~1.5 years old) on a prominent/high-traffic brand domain
long_exposure_duplicate_prior.do_not: suppress_drafting — the finding may still be valid and may earn duplicate points (Bugcrowd P1/P2). Duplicate-risk is partially unavoidable since private reports are invisible.
long_exposure_duplicate_prior.rationale: A service publicly reachable and archive-indexed for years on a major brand has a near-certain prior-report probability. Surface the duplicate-risk so the operator can calibrate effort and expectation, but still draft if the finding is valid. Same long-exposure-duration duplicate signal as the secret-side rule history_only_test_fixture_low_impact-9d2e1, generalized to exposed services.
long_exposure_duplicate_prior.reason: GROUND TRUTH: Bugcrowd flashpaper.chime.com submission was ACCEPTED AS VALID but marked Duplicate of a 2021-10-30 report; the service had Wayback snapshots from 2022-08-03 onward (3+ years public). The finding and report were correct — the only learning is that multi-year archive-indexed exposure on a prominent domain predicts a prior report. Soft signal (annotate, do not skip) because the finding was genuinely valid and duplicate points may still accrue.
